### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
Fresh initialization validates primitive shapes, captures any radiating-boundary reference, fills physical ghosts,
exchanges primitive ghosts and then converts to conserved state.
Absent: initialize from primitives; present: load restart.
Order: code map; no independent measured convergence order.
No defining equation: this section maps control flow or data ownership.
:::

Fresh initialization validates primitive shapes, captures any radiating-boundary reference, fills physical ghosts,
exchanges primitive ghosts and then converts to conserved state. Passive scalar density is seeded using conserved
dry-air density.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path. Numerical operators are derived in
their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

Primitive exchange precedes the equation-of-state conversion, so the conserved ghosts reflect the exchanged
primitives. Solid data are captured and solid velocities reset before the final conserved boundary fill. Mesh
initializes fresh local blocks through concurrent jobs; its restart path instead initializes blocks in a caller-thread
loop. Initialization introduces no independent accuracy order; interpolation and boundary accuracy belong to the
geometry and boundary chapters.

### Limits

The restart branch returns before primitive exchange and relies on saved tensor ghosts. The writer saves full defined
tensors, except the reconstructible scalar ratio. No dedicated fresh-versus-restart ghost equivalence measurement is
supplied.
